{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 18 findings. Ten clauses are compliant (several because the Agreement is silent on burdens the playbook is designed to resist — no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no audit right over us, no liquidated damages, and no auto-renewal trap). Our convenience termination right at 90 days' notice sits at the fallback and needs no change.

Eight items require redlines. Two are critical: the Section 13 indemnity is limited to Losses from breach of Garman's title/rights warranty, with no express defence obligation, no coverage of third-party infringement claims as such and no defence procedure; and Garman owns all IP in the Work including the Modifications developed for us, while our licence back is non-transferable, location-limited and non-sublicensable. Three items are walk-away territory as drafted: the blanket mutual assignment bar with no M&A carve-out, the mutual all-employee no-hire in Section 19, and the complete absence of any vendor insurance covenant despite Garman personnel attending Authorized Locations and handling our data. Section 15 also contains no aggregate monetary cap, leaving our own direct-damages exposure unlimited, and there is no exit assistance or data-return obligation anywhere in the document.

Our asks are targeted: we propose preferred-level positions on indemnity, governing law, insurance and transition, and the shortest fallback-level cure on liability cap, licence transfer, assignment, non-solicitation and warranty remedy.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue and position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Indemnity covers only Losses from breach of Garman's title/rights warranty; no express defence obligation, no third-party infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach or wilful-misconduct coverage, and no defence procedure. Injunction remedies are procure/modify/replace only, with no refund if none is available. **Proposal:** add an express Garman defence/indemnity paragraph with notice, control and cooperation mechanics; cap any Sparkling indemnity to Sparkling-provided content and Sparkling's breach of law. We do not import the fallback super-cap or Customer modification/combination exclusions, as § 15 already carves out § 13 and no such exclusions exist. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Garman owns all IP in the Work, expressly including the Improvements and the Schedule "D" Modifications developed for us; our licence is non-transferable and location-limited, with additional fees for other locations and § 3(c) barring sublicensing. No limit on Garman's use of our converted data. **Proposal:** broaden the § 2 grant to perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free with modify/sublicense rights, conform § 3(c), and limit Garman's use of our data to processing solely to provide the services (Garman retains its software and know-how under § 13). |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 | § 20(d) is a flat mutual consent bar with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard; § 3(c) separately bars us from assigning except as Garman authorizes. Walk-away territory. No change-of-control clause exists, so Garman has no termination or re-pricing right on our change of control. **Proposal (fallback):** mutual successor assignment on written notice; other assignments require consent not unreasonably withheld; conform § 3(c). |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Affiliate coverage and perpetuity (while fees are paid) are already satisfactory, but the licence is "non-transferable", § 3(c) bars transfer of the Work absent Garman's written authorization and § 20(d) requires consent, so there is no path to carry the licence to a successor. **Proposal:** add a successor transfer right in the grant without Garman's approval and conform § 3(c). We deliberately leave § 20(d)'s mutual clause untouched here. |
| 5 | High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | § 15 mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages and mutually carves out § 13 and § 14, but contains no aggregate monetary cap, so each party's direct-damages exposure — including ours — is unlimited. **Proposal (fallback):** add a mutual cap at fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim, with gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap. Existing carve-outs suffice; we do not pursue the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor. |
| 6 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 | § 20(h) selects Nova Scotia and Canadian law with non-exclusive Nova Scotia venue (no arbitration clause anywhere). Nova Scotia is not on the accepted list, so the clause fails both preferred and fallback on law and forum, and non-exclusive venue leaves no certain merits forum. **Proposal (preferred):** New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, carve-out for temporary injunctive relief. Delaware, California or England and Wales remain acceptable fallbacks. |
| 7 | Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 20 General Matters | No insurance covenant anywhere; § 20(a)–(j) ends with the entire-agreement clause. Garman personnel attend Authorized Locations for installation, data conversion and training and handle our data, so an uninsured vendor is walk-away territory. **Proposal (preferred):** insert § 20(k) — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where our data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. |
| 8 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | § 19 is a mutual **no-hire**, not a non-solicit; it reaches "any employee of the other party", runs one year from termination rather than from the end of a person's involvement, and has no advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. A no-hire covering all personnel is walk-away territory. **Proposal (fallback):** 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and an express statement that hiring is not prohibited. |
| 9 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination | No exit clause exists. § 17 covers only our return/destruction of Garman's materials and a fee refund on Garman default; § 8 return of our Confidential Information applies only on pre-acceptance rejection; § 16 escrow gives source-code continuity but no transition assistance or data return. **Proposal (preferred):** insert § 17(d) — up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter. § 18 survival already carries the obligation. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | The one-year software conformance warranty exceeds the 90-day floor, but (i) no warranty of any duration covers Garman's services (installation, training, Maintenance Services) and (ii) § 12 states no remedy — § 10(c) is a best-efforts repair conditional on paid maintenance, and the §§ 7–8 money-back mechanic is confined to the acceptance period, is "in lieu of any other remedy" and terminates the Agreement. **Proposal:** add a 30-day services warranty and an express repair/replace-or-refund remedy for the § 12 warranties. No general disclaimer exists, so the express warranty is not swallowed. |
| 11 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity, sole-supplier or minimum-requirements obligation. Every use of "exclusive" runs in our favour or is unrelated (non-exclusive licence, non-exclusive escrow licence, exclusive remedies in § 15, non-exclusive jurisdiction in § 20(h)); § 19 is an employee covenant, not exclusive dealing. No redline. |
| 12 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalty, minimum fee or early-termination charge on us. § 11 obliges payment only of Fee Schedule amounts; § 17(b) convenience exit carries no fee; termination for Garman's default converts the licence to perpetual with a refund of prepaid fees. Chargeable repair services for Sparkling-caused faults are a service charge, not a penalty. No redline. |
| 13 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint. § 3 and paragraph (g) impose only ordinary licence-scope limits; we remain free to acquire or develop competing routing software. § 19 is addressed separately. Preferred position met. |
| 14 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17(b) gives us an unconditional 90-day convenience exit with no early-termination fee or accelerated payment; Garman has no convenience right at all (§ 17(c) is insolvency/uncured default only). Sits at the fallback; noted short of preferred only on the 90-day notice period and the absence of an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on our convenience exit. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No audit, inspection, verification or usage-monitoring right binds us. § 14 defines Confidential Information to include accounting records "for which access is obtained" but grants no access right. Better than preferred; proposing audit parameters would create a right that does not exist. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN mechanic in either direction; § 11 states our entire pricing obligation as payment of Fee Schedule amounts, with no no-less-favourable, disclosure or price-matching language. Preferred position met. |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No minimum purchase, volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic. § 11 covers Fee Schedule amounts only; § 2 charges extra only if we elect additional locations; § 10 maintenance is a renewable one-year term; § 17(a)/(b) keep the licence alive while fees are paid with a 90-day exit. Revisit only if Schedule "A" introduces committed licence counts or maintenance years. |
| 18 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 10 Maintenance and Support | The only renewal mechanic is a "renewable one-year term" of maintenance; no automatic renewal, no non-renewal notice window on us, and no price-uplift mechanic (§ 10 maintenance is "without additional fees or charges"). Noted short of preferred only in the absence of express mutual-written-agreement renewal wording and a CPI/3% cap; minor sub-elements, not deviations. No redline. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following three items are identified in our verified findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Assignment (Page 10 / § 20(d), with § 3(c))** — a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. We require, at minimum, mutual successor assignment on written notice, with § 3(c) conformed.
2. **Non-solicitation (§ 19)** — a mutual no-hire covering all personnel of the other party. We require conversion to a 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
3. **Vendor insurance (§ 20 General Matters)** — no insurance covenant of any kind while Garman personnel attend Authorized Locations and handle our data. We require the § 20(k) covenant described above.

In addition, the two critical findings — the § 13 indemnity and the § 2 IP/licence position — go to the core risk allocation of the deal and should not be conceded without escalation, even though they are not themselves flagged as walk-away.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight actionable items: § 13 (defence and indemnity), § 2 and § 3(c) (licence scope, successor transfer, data use), § 20(d) (assignment), § 15 (mutual 12-month fees cap), § 20(h) (New York law and exclusive New York County courts), new § 20(k) (insurance), § 19 (non-solicit), new § 17(d) (transition and data return) and § 12 (services warranty and remedy).
2. **Sequence the negotiation**: lead with the three walk-away items and the two critical findings; hold the liability cap, governing law, warranty remedy and transition clause as the second tranche, where we have identified fallback landing zones (Delaware / California / England and Wales for governing law; fallback-level cap and non-solicit already reflected in our draft).
3. **Obtain Schedule "A" and the Fee Schedule**, which are not attached. Our RENEWAL and MINCOMMIT findings are compliant on the face of the Agreement but would need revisiting if the Schedule introduces committed licence counts, committed maintenance years or a quoted renewal-period maintenance uplift.
4. **Confirm business inputs** for the insurance limits (whether Garman will process our data at the volumes assumed for the cyber/privacy layer) and for the transition-assistance period, before we exchange the draft.
5. **Record the positions we are not pursuing** so they are not reopened as concessions: the preferred USD 1,000,000 liability floor and additional preferred carve-outs, the fallback indemnity super-cap and Customer modification/combination exclusions (both worse for us than the current text), the 30-day convenience notice, and audit parameters that would create a Vendor right that does not exist today."}
